stem: A neonate has a supine abdominal x-ray because bowel perforation is being considered, and no free air is seen under the diaphragm. What is the most appropriate interpretation?

options.text: Absence of subdiaphragmatic free air does not exclude free intraperitoneal gas on a supine AXR
The film is normal because the football sign must be present if free gas exists
Free intraperitoneal gas is assessed only with chest radiography
A gasless abdomen would be expected if perforation were present

explanation: Absence of subdiaphragmatic free air does not exclude free intraperitoneal gas on a supine AXR. On a supine film, free air may be difficult to detect, so a negative subdiaphragmatic-air finding does not rule out perforation.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because perforation is not excluded by the absence of subdiaphragmatic free air on a supine AXR.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because free intraperitoneal gas may be present even when no subdiaphragmatic free air is seen on a supine abdominal x-ray.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because the football sign is one possible sign of free gas, but its absence does not make the film normal or exclude perforation.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because abdominal x-ray is used to assess for free intraperitoneal gas; chest radiography is not the only relevant imaging test.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a gasless abdomen is not the expected definitive finding for perforation and does not reliably confirm or exclude it.
